sm: The show opens with headlines: Nvidia's board refuses to bring back its former CEO, Anthropic's IPO, and House Democrats choosing their leader. Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress says the board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation and will not reinstate him, despite pressure from tech figures including Elon Musk and Pavel Durov over news of his affairs. Anthropic is considering expanding its IPO after reported institutional interest of 400 billion dollars and nearly 100 billion from retail investors, which could push pricing above the 70 to 78 dollar range. A Government Accountability Office test found four major AI chatbots could be manipulated into producing detailed attack plans, though the companies say they are strengthening safeguards. Xi Jinping greeted Trump at the airport in Shenzhen ahead of a possible meeting with Putin. House Democrats backed Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker, 251 to 11, despite resistance from seven incoming members who want stronger commitments on Medicare for All and abolishing ICE.

Texas Lieutenant Governor-elect Vicki Goodwin, who campaigned against a data center crisis, named lobbyist Leticia Van Deputte co-chair of her transition team. She is one of seven lobbyists on the 14-person team, and has clients including Vantage Data Centers. The Daily Wire reports that a Soros-funded think tank, Groundwork Collaborative, produced a dossier listing companies such as Apple, Microsoft, Oracle, SpaceX, JetBlue and McDonald's as possible investigation targets for incoming congressional Democrats. Waymo has banned its cars from freeways after the California DMV ordered a halt pending investigation, following incidents in construction zones and near police. Expert Philip Koopman called the ban the right choice but said it hurts airport business. Finally, Grand Theft Auto 6 is expected to earn three to five billion dollars in its first week, topping Grand Theft Auto 5's records, and launches at midnight tonight.
